overlaps.locator: Supplementary Fig. S22 caption, printed p.42; Supplementary Materials, Estimating global epistasis, printed p.19.
overlaps.quote: Panel (A) demonstrates a nonlinear function (blue line), mapping the sum of first-order predictors onto the fitness of 24,542 variants with the Asp27/Glu27/Cys27 genotype.
overlaps.definition_quote: We detected the presence of global epistasis as a nonlinear dependence between fitness values and the sum of linear predictors of the first order (72). To this end, we estimated first-order additive effects of each allele for each position using a linear regression model. We sum the first order effects and mapped them to fitness values of corresponding variants via a nonlinear monotonically increasing function. In particular, we used I-splines basis functions (72).
overlaps.definition_divergence: The panel-A statistic is a fitted first-order I-spline mapping, for which the live GraphFLA metric inventory has no equivalent. The caption does not state the nucleotide-level codon filter: NOT STATED IN PAPER. As an input-side count check, the full RAW CSV contains 24,542 Asp/Glu/Cys-at-27 records, while the trusted processed component CSV contains 23,745; 797 group members are absent from that component input. The latter file-derived counts are NOT STATED IN PAPER.

overlaps.locator: Supplementary Materials, Determining nonfunctional mutations, printed pp.14–15; Analysis of the fitness landscape—Constructing a network of variants, printed p.15; Supplementary Fig. S22 caption, printed p.42.
overlaps.quote: This connected subgraph of variants is the fitness landscape we analyze. It contains 135,178 variants and 324,044 edges between them.
overlaps.definition_quote:
Exclude pairs where both variants are nonfunctional (i.e., their fitness is below the cut-off)
Construct a network by connecting each pair of neighboring variants with a directed edge (arrow). Any one such edge corresponds to a fitness-increasing mutation, i.e., it points from the variant with lower fitness to the neighbor with higher fitness.
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper defines each fitness-increasing mutation as one directed edge after excluding neighbor pairs where both variants are nonfunctional. The cutoff quote is Supplementary Materials, Determining nonfunctional mutations, printed pp.14–15: ‘This procedure resulted in a relative fitness cut-off of 𝑟 𝑖 − 𝑟 WT = -0.507774.’ Building the trusted processed input with that filter reproduces the same directed edge population. Independent direct one-nucleotide neighbor enumeration yielded the identical oriented pair set.

overlaps.locator: Supplementary Fig. S22 caption, printed p.42; Supplementary Materials, Estimating global epistasis, printed p.19.
overlaps.quote: The fitness gain of beneficial mutations (vertical axis) decreases in genetic backgrounds with higher fitness (horizontal axis). The blue line represents a linear regression model (fitness gain is the response variable and the fitness of the genetic background is the predictor variable). N=324,044 mutations. (B) shows a magnified part of (C).
overlaps.definition_quote: The blue line represents a linear regression model (fitness gain is the response variable and the fitness of the genetic background is the predictor variable). N=324,044 mutations.
overlaps.definition_divergence: Panel B/C is an edge-level ordinary least squares regression using one observation per beneficial mutation. GraphFLA's docstring states: ‘This function quantifies this trend by calculating the correlation between the fitness of each genotype (node) and the average fitness improvement provided by its direct successors (fitter one-mutant neighbors).’ Locator: graphfla/analysis/epistasis/idiosyncrasy.py, lines 263–270. Its signature is ‘method: Literal["pearson", "spearman", "regression"] = "pearson"’ (lines 259–262). Thus the default DRI collapses multiple outgoing edges from one background into one node-level mean and weights source backgrounds once; the panel regression weights each mutation edge. The two outputs have different statistics and units. Their negative signs agree, but the DRI is not a faithful numeric summary of the plotted slope.

overlaps.reason: The paper plots the regression but does not state its slope, intercept, or correlation: NOT STATED IN PAPER. Computed reconstruction, not a printed target; fitness gain was operationalized as fitter-endpoint fitness minus background fitness, and the paper's gain equation is NOT STATED IN PAPER. Panel B from direct neighbor enumeration: slope=-0.432920741883921, intercept=0.43477401242456315, correlation=-0.4764872794862937, n=324044. Panel C from the GraphFLA edge list: slope=-0.43292074188392254, intercept=0.4347740124245627, correlation=-0.47648727948629294, n=324044. B/C edge sets are identical. GraphFLA has 134664 unique source backgrounds with improving edges; this file-derived count is NOT STATED IN PAPER. GraphFLA DRI was computed successfully, but it uses a different aggregation and statistic.

verdict_reason: The paper's printed 324,044 beneficial-mutation population is exactly the filtered directed edge set reproduced by GraphFLA. The full raw input confirms the Fig. S22A subset count, while the trusted processed component omits some members. Panels B/C coefficients are plot-only and were reconstructed from the input. GraphFLA's DRI is negative but is not the same statistic or weighting as the edge-level regression slope.
